text:
alex-w: Quick sync — thinking about attribute resolution for ingest. do we do a lookup at edge (stamp attributes early) or leave keys and resolve in enrichment?

maria-k: +1 to discuss. my concern with early stamping is correctness under retries and replays. what if the lookup service is flaky?

cheng-y: also cost. doing lookups at edge multiplies calls across many clients. late enrichment centralizes calls and caches.

sam-t: late enrichment helps batching and reduces reads, but splits responsibility: query shapes change and consumers may expect immediate attributes for routing. e.g., billing key used by quota middlewares.

lisa-p: can we split responsibilities? stamp a minimal routing key at edge (cheap hash) and resolve full attributes later for billing and analytics?

alex-w: that split is what i've been leaning toward. tiny routing token at edge (hash+tenant) — deterministic so retries idempotent. full attribute lookup in enrich with a TTL to escape staleness.

maria-k: sounds reasonable. we need to define the shape of that routing token. what fields are allowed? should it be stable across SDK versions?

cheng-y: propose: routing_token = base64(sha256(service_id || tenant_id || short_event_id)). keep it opaque. avoid adding hi-card fields.

sam-t: on the enrichment side we need fallback semantics: if the external attrib service is down, we should tag events as unresolved and still ingest, with a retry/backfill job to patch later. otherwise we drop and cause customer-visible gaps.

lisa-p: +1 to backfill. but backfill must be bounded in retention and cost. define SLA: backfill window 7 days, and patch only if event retention still available.

alex-w: good point. also thinking about the idempotency key so backfills don't double-apply costs. enrichment patch should be upsert by event id.

ingest-bot: reminder: we've rolled out schema v12 that reserves attributes.stamp_token (string) and attributes.resolution_state (enum: unresolved, resolved, backfilled). please use these fields.

maria-k: one more tradeoff: cardinality explosion if we enrich with high-cardinality attributes pre-ingest. we should avoid attaching large attribute sets until after sampling filters.

cheng-y: suggestion: enrichment pipeline stages: 1) stamp routing_token at edge, 2) sample/drop decisions, 3) batch lookup for resolved attrs, 4) attach resolved attrs and mark resolved. samples marked unresolved go to backfill queue.

sam-t: OK. action items: cheng to prototype routing_token generator and cache policy, lisa to write backfill job spec and cost estimate, maria to draft SDK guidance for stamping, alex to capture SLA decisions in the RFC.

lisa-p: I'll add a small sketch of the backfill coordination in the runbook — how ops detect backfill lag and how we surface failed patches.

alex-w: thanks. if no objections i'll book a 30m follow-up tomorrow to review prototypes.

maria-k: fine by me.

cheng-y: works for me.

sam-t: ✅

ingest-bot: deploy note: enrich-v3 staged to canary, uses batch-lookup client v2. track metrics: lookup_success_rate, unresolved_count, backfill_queue_length.
